title: Multiplication and Division: Groups, Arrays, Sharing and Remainders
seo_title: Grade 3 Multiplication and Division Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve and explain solutions to practical problems that involve equal sharing and grouping with whole numbers up to 100 and with answers that may include remainders; multiplication and division of whole numbers to 100.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 3 maths worksheets: equal groups, arrays, sharing, remainders and multiplication and division stories. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Groups: number of groups × number in each group.
  • Sharing: total ÷ number of shares = number in each share.
  • Grouping: total ÷ size of each group = number of groups.
  • What is left is the remainder: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2.

Examples

Example

23 eggs into boxes of 6

6, 12, 18

Answer: 3 boxes, 5 left over

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Groups or eachRead what the question asks.
The remainderSay what is left over.
The order24 ÷ 6, not 6 ÷ 24.

The class sets up chairs in the gym. There are 6 rows. Each row has 8 chairs. How many chairs are there?
items.e: There are 6 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 6 × 8 = 48. Adding 6 + 8 = 14 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: At camp, 7 canoes go out on the lake. Each canoe holds 3 people. How many people can the canoes hold?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 3, so multiply: 7 × 3 = 21. Adding 7 + 3 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Karabo skates 4 laps around the rink each day. How many laps does she skate in 7 days?
items.e: There are 7 equal groups of 4, so multiply: 7 × 4 = 28. Adding 7 + 4 = 11 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: Each ringette team has 6 players on the ice. 4 teams line up on the ice for a photo. How many players is that?
items.e: There are 4 equal groups of 6, so multiply: 4 × 6 = 24. Adding 4 + 6 = 10 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: At lunch, 8 learners sit at each table. There are 9 full tables. How many learners are at the tables?
items.e: There are 9 equal groups of 8, so multiply: 9 × 8 = 72. Adding 9 + 8 = 17 only joins the two numbers.

items.q: In gym class, 30 learners make teams of 5. How many teams are there?
items.e: Grouping in 5s: 30 ÷ 5. 5 × 6 = 30, so there are 6 teams.

items.q: There are 56 chairs in the gym. They are in 7 equal rows. How many chairs are in each row?
items.e: 56 chairs in 7 equal rows: 56 ÷ 7. 7 × 8 = 56, so each row has 8 chairs.

items.q: 32 learners go on a field trip. Each parent driver takes 4 learners. How many cars are needed?
items.e: Groups of 4: 32 ÷ 4. 4 × 8 = 32, so 8 cars are needed.

Priya finds 4 shells at the beach. Refilwe finds 5 times as many. How many shells does Refilwe find?
items.e: 5 times as many as 4 means 5 × 4 = 20. 9 is 5 + 4, which adds instead of multiplies.
